description: Frontier Readiness diagnostic instrument — a parallel assessment to controls.json that measures organizational capacity to scale AI agents across the five Capability Drivers (AI Strategy & Experience, Business Strategy, AI Governance & Security, Technology & Data, Organization & Culture) on the 100-500 maturity scale. This manifest does NOT replace the 78-control technical assessment; it supplements it by surfacing the scale-breaker driver that limits Frontier Transformation Pattern readiness. Most questions in v1 remain facilitator-collected, with a limited telemetry-backed subset enabled where collector signals are available; remaining pass_condition strings preserve future evaluator expansion paths. Maturity levels (100 Initial / 200 Repeatable / 300 Defined / 400 Capable / 500 Optimized) and pattern_target_profiles align to docs/framework/agentic-capability-drivers.md and docs/framework/transformation-patterns.md.

drivers.name: AI Strategy & Experience
drivers.description: AI portfolio governance — how the firm decides what to build, sponsor, and sunset.
drivers.fsi_translation: Portfolio rationalization with named executive sponsors per pattern, published enterprise AI strategy reviewed by the Governance Committee, board-level reporting on the agent portfolio, and documented sunset criteria for agents that fail to demonstrate value.

drivers.name: Business Strategy
drivers.description: Business value alignment — how AI investments are tied to named outcomes, KPIs, and accountable business owners per use case.
drivers.primary_owner: Executive Sponsor (CEO / COO) with Business Owners per use case
drivers.fsi_translation: Formal process redesign documentation for production agents, named business owners per use case, KPI dashboards reviewed in the governance cadence, and version-controlled decision rules with named human supervisors for core regulated processes (KYC, claims, financial close, regulatory reporting).

drivers.name: AI Governance & Security
drivers.description: Risk management and control posture — how the firm maintains examiner-defensible governance over the agent estate.
drivers.primary_owner: Joint: Chief Risk Officer, Chief Compliance Officer, CISO; AI Governance Lead operates the day-to-day program
drivers.fsi_translation: Zone-classified Managed Environments, comprehensive audit logging at FINRA 4511 / SEC 17a-4 retention thresholds, supervision under FINRA Rule 3110 by named principals, model risk tiering per OCC Bulletin 2026-13 (formerly OCC 2011-12) / Fed SR 26-2, bias and fairness assessment before consumer-impacting deployment, and predictive governance with human-in-the-loop change control.

drivers.name: Technology & Data
drivers.description: Platform and data engineering — environments, identity, telemetry pipelines, RAG corpus integrity, and observability.
drivers.primary_owner: Power Platform Admin and platform engineering teams, accountable to the CTO
drivers.fsi_translation: Environment Groups with tier classification, automated agent inventory, SIEM integration (Sentinel), RAG source integrity validation for production agents, item-level permission scanning of knowledge sources, identity managed under Entra Agent ID, and integrated telemetry sufficient for incident reconstruction.

drivers.name: Organization & Culture
drivers.description: Workforce enablement and change — supervisor training, maker community, AI-positive but compliance-aware culture.
drivers.primary_owner: AI Governance Lead partnered with HR / Change Management; supervisor accountability per FINRA Rule 3110
drivers.fsi_translation: Role-based training covering supervisors, makers, end users, and customer-facing personnel; user consent and AI disclosure enforcement; communication compliance monitoring updated for AI-generated content; trained-supervisor culture with documented per-decision review obligations and continuous-improvement discipline within change control.

questions.question_text: Has the organization identified at least one named individual responsible for AI initiative oversight, even if only informally?
questions.fsi_context: Examiners begin with 'who is accountable for AI?' An identifiable owner is the minimum starting point for any AI program; without one, the firm cannot answer the first supervisory question.

questions.question_text: Within at least one business unit, do AI agent investments follow recurring, documented patterns (intake request, sponsor sign-off, inventory entry) that staff can describe consistently?
questions.fsi_context: A repeatable intake pattern in one business unit demonstrates the firm has moved beyond ad-hoc experimentation. This evidence is the threshold for L200 and supports later enterprise rollout under FINRA 3110 supervision expectations.

questions.question_text: Has the organization published an enterprise AI strategy reviewed by a Governance Committee, with a portfolio-level inventory of in-scope agents and named executive sponsors per Frontier Transformation Pattern?
questions.fsi_context: A defined enterprise AI strategy with portfolio governance helps meet OCC Bulletin 2026-13 (formerly OCC 2011-12) model risk expectations and gives examiners a documented chain of accountability from sponsor to agent.
questions.notes: Auto-evaluator capped at 'partial' — site naming heuristic detects strategy publication, but governance review + portfolio scope are facilitator-only.

questions.question_text: Is the AI strategy refreshed on a documented cadence aligned to the firm's governance cadence, with portfolio-level reporting reaching the board or board-designated committee?
questions.fsi_context: Capable maturity requires the AI strategy to be a living document with board visibility, supporting Fed SR 26-2 (formerly SR 11-7) expectations for senior governance over model risk and helping meet OCC Bulletin 2026-13 oversight requirements.

questions.question_text: Do named executive sponsors provide quarterly outcome attestation for each pattern in the portfolio, with documented, audit-trail-ready sunset criteria for agents that fail to demonstrate value?
questions.fsi_context: Optimized AI strategy at FSI scale requires audit-trail-ready sponsor attestation and documented sunset criteria. Without these, examiners cannot reconstruct portfolio decisions over the FINRA 4511 / SEC 17a-4 retention window.

questions.question_text: Have any deployed AI agents been assigned a business owner accountable for the outcomes of the work the agent supports?
questions.fsi_context: At Initial maturity the basic question is whether anyone outside IT owns the business outcome of an agent. Without a named business owner, no KPI tracking or process redesign is possible.

questions.question_text: Within a single business line, are agent use cases tied to informal but identifiable outcome targets (e.g., handle time, throughput, accuracy) that the team reviews periodically?
questions.fsi_context: Repeatable maturity requires at least one business line to track agent outcomes against targets, even informally. This evidence supports later formalization into KPI dashboards reviewed in the governance cadence.

questions.question_text: Are formal process redesign artifacts maintained for production agents, with named business owners per use case and KPI dashboards reviewed in the governance cadence?
questions.fsi_context: Defined maturity requires process redesign documentation that examiners can review for any regulated workflow touched by an agent. KPI dashboards provide the operating evidence behind the redesign and support OCC Bulletin 2026-13 model use documentation.

questions.question_text: Are end-to-end agent-supported services governed by documented decision boundaries, escalation rules, and SLAs, with performance and cost attribution integrated into operational reporting and a documented executive review cadence?
questions.fsi_context: Capable maturity ties agent operations to executive operational reviews, supporting SOX 404 internal control assertions over financially material processes and giving the risk committee operating telemetry on agent-supported work.

questions.question_text: Do agents in core business processes (KYC, claims, financial close, regulatory reporting) operate under version-controlled decision rules with named human supervisors per FINRA Rule 3110, where material change to the process is documented as triggering a governance review?
questions.fsi_context: Optimized business strategy maturity for core regulated processes requires versioned decision rules and named supervisors to support FINRA 3110 supervision and SEC 17a-4 record reconstruction. The supervisor — not the agent — remains the accountable decision-maker.

questions.question_text: Does the organization have any informal guardrails (acceptable use guidance, basic DLP, training reminders) addressing AI agent use, even if not platform-enforced?
questions.fsi_context: Initial maturity requires at minimum some informal guardrails for AI use. Without them the firm cannot demonstrate any awareness of GLBA 501(b) Safeguards or FINRA supervisory expectations for AI-assisted work.

questions.question_text: In some business units, are platform controls (DLP, audit logging) applied to agents handling sensitive data, with a written AI policy that staff can locate and reference?
questions.fsi_context: Repeatable maturity requires applied platform controls in at least some business units plus a discoverable AI policy. This is the foundation for later enterprise-wide enforcement supporting FINRA 4511 record requirements and GLBA Safeguards.

questions.question_text: Are agents classified into Zone-tiered Managed Environments with comprehensive audit logging at the FINRA 4511 / SEC 17a-4 retention threshold, supervision under FINRA Rule 3110 by named principals, and model risk tiering per OCC Bulletin 2026-13 (formerly OCC 2011-12) for regulated agents?
questions.fsi_context: Defined maturity requires zone-classified environments, retention-grade audit logging, named supervisors, and model risk tiering — the four evidence pillars an FSI examiner will request first when reviewing AI agent governance.
questions.notes: Auto-evaluator caps suggested answer at 'partial' because model-risk overlay (the third L300 signal) is not telemetry-verifiable. Facilitator must confirm model risk separately to upgrade to 'yes'.

questions.question_text: Do risk metrics flow into a risk committee on a documented cadence, supported by Sentinel detection content, an adversarial testing program, bias and fairness assessment before consumer-impacting deployment, and tested incident response runbooks?
questions.fsi_context: Capable maturity requires the risk committee to receive operating telemetry and tested response runbooks. Reg B / ECOA bias testing before consumer-impacting deployment helps meet fair-lending defense expectations under CFPB scrutiny.

questions.question_text: Does the organization operate continuous control monitoring with risk-tier-based release gates, hallucination feedback driving change-managed retraining gated by independent validation, and quarterly examiner readiness drills?
questions.fsi_context: Optimized governance for FSI is predictive monitoring with human-in-the-loop change control. Quarterly examiner readiness drills convert governance posture into operating muscle memory before a real exam arrives, supporting FINRA 3110 and OCC Bulletin 2026-13 defensibility.

questions.question_text: Is there any visibility into which Power Platform environments host AI agents, even if maintained as a manual list?
questions.fsi_context: Initial maturity requires at minimum awareness of where agents run. Without environment visibility the firm cannot scope retention or telemetry to support FINRA 4511 / SEC 17a-4 books-and-records expectations.

questions.question_text: Are some environments tagged or grouped for agent workloads, with basic telemetry (sign-in logs, agent execution records) collected and retained on a defined schedule?
questions.fsi_context: Repeatable maturity requires environment grouping and baseline telemetry collection. This is the foundation for later SIEM integration and incident reconstruction supporting GLBA 501(b) Safeguards and FINRA 4511 retention.

questions.question_text: Are Environment Groups with tier classification operational, with automated agent inventory, SIEM integration, RAG source integrity validation for production agents, item-level permission scanning at deployment, and documented data lineage?
questions.fsi_context: Defined maturity requires the substrate evidence stack — tiered environments, automated inventory, SIEM, RAG integrity, and lineage — that examiners use to verify the data the agent retrieved is the record under FINRA 4511 / SEC 17a-4.
questions.notes: Auto-evaluator capped at 'partial' — 3/5 signals are telemetry-verifiable (env groups, SIEM, SP scan), but agent inventory is not collected and RAG-integrity + lineage are facilitator-only.

questions.question_text: Does the platform provide integrated telemetry across Sentinel, the Agent 365 Observability SDK, and Copilot Hub, with reusable agent templates curated by the CoE and identity governed under Entra Agent ID?
questions.fsi_context: Capable platform maturity gives operations and audit teams a single integrated telemetry view with managed agent identity, supporting incident reconstruction and FINRA 3110 supervisory review of agent-assisted work.

questions.question_text: Is the platform continuously monitored and version-controlled, with multi-agent orchestration governed by documented architecture, enforced orchestration limits, retraining gated by independent validation, and grounding data integrity verified on every release under change management?
questions.fsi_context: Optimized platform maturity for FSI requires verified grounding integrity per release plus enforced orchestration limits — the technical preconditions for examiner-defensible multi-agent deployment under OCC Bulletin 2026-13 and Fed SR 26-2 (formerly SR 11-7).

questions.question_text: Has any baseline AI awareness communication (e.g., acceptable use email, intranet page, kickoff memo) been issued to staff using or potentially using AI agents?
questions.fsi_context: Initial maturity requires at least one documented awareness communication. Without it the firm cannot demonstrate that staff were on notice of AI policy expectations under FINRA 3110 supervisory standards.

questions.question_text: Does a general AI training module exist that staff in pilot business units have completed, with informal maker channels (e.g., a Teams community of practice) where users share patterns?
questions.fsi_context: Repeatable maturity requires evidence of completed training in pilot units and an informal maker community. These are the precursors to role-based enablement at L300 and supervisor accountability under FINRA 3110.

questions.question_text: Is a role-based training and awareness program operational covering supervisors, makers, end users, and customer-facing personnel, with user consent and AI disclosure enforcement live and communication compliance monitoring updated for AI-generated content?
questions.fsi_context: Defined maturity requires role-differentiated training and updated communication compliance monitoring. Supervisor training discharges FINRA 3110 obligations; disclosure enforcement supports FINRA 2210 communications standards and Reg B adverse-action notice expectations.

questions.question_text: Is there a curated maker community with documented contribution paths and KPIs, certified maker pathways, customer AI disclosure and marketing-claims governance applied to all external surfaces, and supervisor training records evidenced for examination?
questions.fsi_context: Capable culture maturity converts informal practice into examiner-evidenced training records and external-surface governance. Maker KPIs and certification provide the operating signal that culture is institutionalized rather than aspirational.

questions.question_text: Can the organization demonstrate to an examiner that the supervisor — not the agent — is accountable for any decision the agent supported, with continuous-improvement discipline operationalized within change control and documented per-decision review obligations?
questions.fsi_context: Optimized FSI culture maturity is trained-supervisor accountability under change control. The L500 reframing for FSI explicitly rejects 'AI-first' framing in favor of supervisor-led continuous improvement, supporting FINRA 3110 supervision and OCC Bulletin 2026-13 model use governance.
